newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine bank plans $200-mln Samurai bonds.
newsitem.headline: Philippine bank plans $200-mln Samurai bonds.

text.p: State-owned Development Bank of the Philippines plans to issue about $200 million worth of Samurai bonds to fund its housing loans, a Department of Finance official said on Monday.

The proceeds, expected to total five billion pesos, is one-third of the yearly 15 billion-peso requirements for low-cost housing, the official, who declined to be identified, said in a telephone interview.
The official said the bank plans to launch the yen-denominated bonds in the next few months. The bonds may carry a rate of not more than three percent and a payment period of at least five years.
"The earliest will be in April," the official said, referring to the time table of the launching.
The Japanese market is being tapped because of the low interest rates prevailing in that market, he said.
He said proceeds of the Samurai bond will serve as bridge financing until a more sustainable source of funding can be obtained for the housing loans.
He said the government may set up an institution to be jointly owned by the public and private sectors that will provide secondary mortgage financing for housing.
